create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl (string) as alternative.

oidc_jwt.description: The UserInfo endpoint is intended for authorized user access tokens, not generic client or machine tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Using a machine/client token can fail or omit user identity claims without indicating a security bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization-specific reserved scopes intentionally enforce organization membership and can cause login failure for users outside the selected organization.
oidc_jwt.note: Such failures are expected policy enforcement, not identity confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo returns claims depending on granted scopes; many fields are omitted unless corresponding scopes were requested.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing email/profile/metadata/roles claims is by design when scopes were not granted, not evidence of identity confusion or claim stripping.

oidc_jwt.description: Token introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An active=false result can reflect audience scoping rather than token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: Reserved project audience scopes intentionally add project IDs to the access token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Extra aud values are by design when these scopes are requested.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active=true only when the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive introspection result can reflect audience mismatch of the introspecting client rather than token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer assertions are documented as signed JWTs submitted to the token endpoint, but the docs do not describe jti tracking or one-time-use semantics for assertions.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token or missing jti as a vulnerability by default; treat as stateless JWT behavior unless the same assertion is documented as single-use elsewhere.

oidc_jwt.description: Token revocation endpoint requires client authentication depending on the configured authorization method.
oidc_jwt.note: Revocation failures without proper client auth are expected and should not be interpreted as inability to revoke tokens.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT profile grant assertions are documented as standard JWT bearer grants with signature, issuer/audience, exp, and iat checks, but no jti replay tracking requirement is documented.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same valid JWT assertion may be accepted by design unless a separate one-time-use mechanism is documented; do not flag replay_same_token as a vulnerability from docs alone.

oidc_jwt.description: The redirect_uri used at token exchange must exactly match the redirect_uri used in the authorization request and a preregistered URI.
oidc_jwt.note: Mismatched redirect_uri causing invalid_grant is by design, not a flow-coherence bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Invalid response_mode values are ignored and ZITADEL falls back to the default response mode for the configured response type.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not interpret fallback behavior as parameter injection acceptance or flow confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection only reports active=true when the requesting client is authorized and part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: An inactive/401 introspection result can be caused by the introspecting client context rather than token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include temporal claims relative to runtime, not hardcoded values: use exp={{now_epoch_plus_N}} for control tokens and exp={{now_epoch_minus_N}} or nbf={{now_epoch_plus_N}} for attack tokens. Without a valid control login in the same setup, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken client/service-account configuration.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN} in docs examples). Do NOT use the token endpoint URL as the sole audience when testing signature or issuer validation, or failures may reflect audience mismatch rather than the intended invariant.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Freshness tests must keep control assertions within the 1h window using iat={{now_epoch}}; otherwise rejection may be due to stale assertion age rather than exp/nbf handling.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT header MUST contain kid matching the downloaded keyId. When testing resign_attacker_key or kid-related attacks, preserve a valid kid/key relationship for control requests; otherwise failures may be caused by key lookup failure instead of signature verification behavior.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used at start_oidc_auth. ZITADEL requires an exact match and returns invalid_grant when the redirection URI differs, so any mismatch rejection is by design and should be asserted as flow binding, not identity confusion.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, start_oidc_auth MUST use code_challenge_method=S256; this is the only supported algorithm. Do NOT test alternate PKCE methods as security findings for ZITADEL because unsupported methods are rejected by design.

For pkce_skip and related I3 tests, a valid control sequence MUST include start_oidc_auth with code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256, then exchange_code_for_token with the matching code_verifier and client_id. Compare attack behavior against this control; otherwise token exchange failure may simply reflect missing PKCE inputs.

For OIDC authorization requests, nonce is REQUIRED for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. For replay-sensitive tests involving id_token validation or request correlation, always send a nonce in start_oidc_auth and verify the returned id_token carries it in control runs; otherwise missing nonce may weaken the oracle and blur I2 conclusions.

For OIDC flow coherence tests, state SHOULD be sent on start_oidc_auth and must be tracked through the callback. Without state, state-swap and cross-session callback confusion tests cannot be interpreted reliably because ZITADEL documents state as the CSRF/session correlation value returned unmodified.

For token_exchange I5 audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is by design and should not be reported as a bug; use a control exchange with a valid subset audience first.

For token_exchange wrong-audience and ignore-audience tests, subject_token_type and actor_token_type MUST be chosen from ZITADEL's supported token-type matrix. Unsupported token types or disallowed combinations (for example refresh_token as subject_token, or jwt without required actor_token) cause by-design rejection and invalidate the oracle.

For token_exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope may be rejected when it exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner, as documented by invalid_scope. Use a control exchange with equal-or-narrower scope first; only treat successful expansion beyond upstream authorization as an I5 issue.

For introspect_token, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. Do NOT interpret active=false for a valid token as token invalidity unless the introspecting client is confirmed to be in aud; otherwise the result reflects audience scoping by design.

For verify_granted_identity, use a user access token, not a client credentials or pure machine token. ZITADEL documents /oidc/v1/userinfo as returning information about the authorized user and requiring the access_token of the user; using a non-user token can fail or omit identity claims for by-design reasons.

For reserved-scope audience tests, adding scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud or urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud intentionally adds project IDs to the access-token aud claim. Do NOT treat the presence of these extra audiences as audience over-grant unless the test itself requested no such reserved scope.

For organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} intentionally enforces organization membership and may fail if the user is outside that org/domain. Use these scopes only when the test intends org scoping; otherwise omit them to avoid false negatives.

For I4 multi-identity tests, preferred_username and username values in ZITADEL are login names of the form username@primarydomain, while sub is the stable subject identifier. Use sub as the primary identity oracle and treat username/preferred_username as display/login attributes that may legitimately differ from the sent principal string.

For replay_same_token on login_with_jwt, repeated use of the same JWT bearer assertion is not documented as one-time and JWT jti is only exposed on introspection for access tokens. Do NOT report simple replay acceptance of a stateless JWT bearer assertion as an I2 vulnerability unless the same assertion is documented or configured as single-use elsewhere.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests on authorization code flow, exchange_code_for_token MUST send the exact same redirect_uri used in start_oidc_auth for control requests. ZITADEL requires an exact match and returns invalid_grant when the redirection URI differs, which is by design rather than a session-binding flaw.

For PKCE-based authorization code tests, start_oidc_auth MUST set code_challenge_method=S256; this is the only supported algorithm. Any other method or omission in a PKCE scenario causes failure by design and must not be interpreted as state/code binding behavior.

For pkce_skip and related OIDC flow tests, omit code_verifier only in the attack request after a control flow that used a valid code_verifier. ZITADEL documents PKCE support and requires the verifier to recompute the challenge; compare HTTP status/error outcomes, not identities.

For OIDC implicit-flow requests (response_type=id_token or id_token token), nonce MUST be provided. Missing nonce in implicit-flow tests is invalid setup and any rejection is by design, not evidence of stronger replay protection than expected.

For OIDC authorization-code controls, the fuzzer SHOULD also send nonce even though docs only recommend it. ZITADEL returns nonce in the ID token when provided, and nonce is required to test replay/session binding correctly; without it, nonce-validation attack patterns are untestable or ambiguous.

For token_exchange audience-binding tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience exceeds that set, rejection is by design and must not be reported as a token-exchange implementation bug.

For token_exchange tests, refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token, actor_token, or requested_token_type. Rejections on refresh-token exchange attempts are by design and must not be treated as evidence of proper audience or scope enforcement.

For introspect_token, the requesting client must be part of the token audience to receive active=true. If active=false for an otherwise valid token, do not infer token invalidity until the introspecting client's audience relationship is confirmed.

For verify_granted_identity, use the access_token of a user, not a client-only token. ZITADEL explicitly documents that /oidc/v1/userinfo expects the user's access token; using a client_credentials-style token or unsuitable machine token can fail by design and must not be interpreted as identity mismatch.

For revocation tests, revoke_session requires client authentication according to the application's configured auth method. A failed revoke without valid client auth is not evidence that tokens are irrevocable; pair each attack with a control revoke using correct client authentication.

For OIDC flow coherence tests using start_oidc_auth, state is only highly recommended, not mandatory. The fuzzer MUST include state in both control and attack requests; otherwise callback correlation and state-swap testing are impossible and missing-state behavior cannot be treated as a vulnerability.

For reserved-scope authorization tests, ZITADEL-specific scopes have exact string semantics with embedded identifiers (for example urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname}, urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud). There is no documented wildcard or pattern mode. For multi-identity or multi-org scenarios, generate exact scope strings per case; do NOT use '*' or glob-like placeholders.

For org-membership authorization tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces organization membership by design. Rejection for non-members is expected and should not be reported as inconsistent audience or claim handling.

For audience-expansion tests, scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds the requested project id to the access-token audience by design. If a token contains that project audience after requesting this scope, do not report it as audience overgrant.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT profile assertion MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, iss equal to sub, exp in the future for the control case, and iat not older than 1 hour. Without a valid control assertion, LOGIN_FAILED may reflect malformed JWT-profile grant construction rather than freshness enforcement.

For JWT profile grant and private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT header MUST include kid set to the downloaded keyId. Omitting kid prevents ZITADEL from identifying the key and can cause false positives in I1 signature-validation tests.

For I1 trust-anchor and issuer-validation tests on login_with_jwt, the assertion aud MUST include the ZITADEL issuing domain. A forged token with wrong aud may be rejected before issuer/signature logic is exercised, so keep aud valid while mutating the targeted field.

For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, iat has an enforced upper age limit: it MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use {{now_epoch}} for control tokens and vary exp/nbf independently; otherwise rejection may be caused by stale iat rather than the intended freshness field.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, redirect_uri matching is exact at both authorize and token exchange. I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests must keep authorize redirect_uri valid and change only the token request redirect_uri to trigger the intended binding check.

For OIDC code-flow tests, state is only highly recommended, not mandatory. The fuzzer MUST supply a unique state anyway for I3 flow-coherence testing; absence of state removes the session-binding oracle and can hide state-swap issues.

For OIDC implicit-flow tests, nonce MUST be provided. For code-flow tests, ZITADEL recommends nonce and returns it in the ID token when provided. The fuzzer SHOULD include nonce in all OIDC auth requests so replay/binding checks are testable and failures are not due to missing required nonce in implicit mode.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx; claims.mdx; authmethods/_implicit.mdx; authmethods/_basic.mdx; authmethods/_pkce.mdx; authmethods/_jwtpk.mdx

oidc_jwt.constraint: For PKCE tests, code_challenge_method supports only exact value S256. Do not fuzz wildcard or alternate methods when testing other invariants; unsupported methods are rejected by design and do not indicate a binding flaw.

For token_exchange scope-escalation tests, invalid_scope may be returned when requested scope exceeds what the resource owner granted. The fuzzer MUST run a control exchange with an equal-or-narrower scope before asserting any escalation behavior.

Token exchange token-type support is restricted: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; requested_token_type jwt is only valid for specific combinations; user_id subject_token is only allowed with actor_token. The fuzzer MUST choose supported token-type combinations or failures are by design.

Introspection success depends on client authorization and audience membership: active=true is only returned when the requesting client is authorized and part of the token audience. A false/401 result does not necessarily mean the token is invalid. Use the same audience-bound client as the token's intended audience for verification.

UserInfo requires an access_token of a user, not a client/service account token. Do not use login_with_jwt service-account access tokens with verify_granted_identity as an identity oracle for human-user semantics; use introspect_token for machine tokens instead.

For refresh-token based exchange_code_for_token tests, requested scope on refresh MUST be a subset of the original scope; omitted scope reuses the original scope. I5 broadening tests must compare against the original authorization and not treat subset enforcement as a bug.
ZITADEL does not support Resource Owner Password Credentials grant. login_with_password is absent for oidc_jwt and must not be synthesized by the fuzzer.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
